Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa, former Delhi Lieutenant-Governor Najeeb Jung, economist Jayati Ghosh and political theorist Rajeev Bhargava are also among the 34 signatories.

While acknowledging that the revised proposals addressed some concerns raised during parliamentary debates and public discussions on the earlier Bills introduced in April 2026, the letter said several serious issues remained unresolved.

The letter invoked the government’s 2014 Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy, which requires draft legislation to be published with explanatory notes for at least 30 days to invite feedback from the public and stakeholders.

items.title: US markets week ahead: Investors eye jobs data, manufacturing & services reports; Salesforce & Marvell earnings in focus
points: Wall Street investors will closely track a series of important US economic indicators in the coming week as markets prepare for the Federal Reserve's December monetary policy decision.
The upcoming economic releases will be among the final major data points for 2026, at a time when households, businesses and policymakers continue to grapple with persistent inflation.
Investors will particularly watch for signs of whether another interest rate increase remains possible at the central bank's next meeting, scheduled for December 8-9.
Salesforce is scheduled to announce its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Wednesday, December 2, after US markets close.
Analysts expect adjusted earnings of $3.45 per share, compared with $3.25 in the corresponding quarter last year, representing growth of approximately 6.2%.
Revenue is projected to increase 11.7% year on year to $11.46 billion.

Analysts expect earnings of $1.10 per share on revenue of $3.15 billion.

items.title: US Military Disables Bulk Carrier Pacific Archer Trying To Breach Iran Blockade
points: Bulk carrier Pacific Archer was left without propulsion in the Gulf of Oman after an American aircraft struck it for trying to slip past the US blockade of Iranian ports.
The strike took place on Thursday and was announced a day later by US Central Command (CENTCOM), which said precision munitions were aimed at the stern of the Palau-flagged ship.
According to the command, the ship had sailed out of Bandar Abbas in Iran and ignored several warnings before it tried to run the blockade.

Built in 2001, the 190-metre bulk carrier is owned by Pacific A Shipping Ltd. and managed by Optimo Marine Ltd. The Pacific Archer is the latest of at least 15 ships that American forces have openly admitted to disabling since April.

items.title: Indian Navy Receives 6,670-Tonne Stealth Frigate INS Vindhyagiri As Final Project 17A Ship

items.title: Russia Says Perm Is World’s First Submarine Armed With Zircon Hypersonic Missiles
points: Russian nuclear-powered submarine Perm has been officially inducted into the Russian Navy as the first boat to carry Zircon hypersonic missiles, Russia claims.
Moscow says the sea-launched Zircon missile can fly at up to nine times the speed of sound and hit targets more than 1,000 kilometres away, making it very hard for air defences to stop.
Russian President Vladimir Putin was on board for the hoisting of the naval flag on November 27 at the Sevmash yard in Severodvinsk in northern Russia.
Built to the Project 885M Yasen-M design, the Perm is the fifth submarine of this upgraded version.
The submarine is also the sixth boat overall in the Yasen family, which also includes the first Project 885 boat, Severodvinsk.
The shipyard laid the keel of the Perm in July 2016 and launched the submarine in March 2025.
Russia first test-fired a Zircon missile from a submerged submarine in 2021 using the lead boat Severodvinsk.

items.title: IMO Lists 587 Ships Under False Flags As Fraudulent Registry Cases Rise Nearly 11%
points: False flag cases listed by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) have reached 587 as the UN agency calls for stronger action against fraudulent ship registries.
Strong national systems and the sharing of information between countries are key to fighting fraudulent registries, IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said on November 25.
He spoke after meeting maritime officials and transport ministers from across Africa at the annual conference of the association of African maritime administrations in Kampala in Uganda.
The conference ran from November 17 to 19 and was attended by heads of ship registries and maritime administrations.
The ship database of the IMO is updated whenever the agency receives information that a vessel is a false flag, and it currently lists 587 such ships.
The figure is nearly 11% higher than the 529 vessels noted by the IMO Legal Committee at its session in April this year.
Close to 40 member states have also informed the IMO that their flags were used fraudulently without their consent or knowledge.
